newsitem.title: USA: TV industry to submit ratings to FCC for review.
newsitem.headline: TV industry to submit ratings to FCC for review.

text.p: The television industry is set to submit its controversial system of rating programs for sex and violence to the Federal Communications Commission for review, officials said Wednesday.
"It could be as early as today. Certainly this week," said Richard Taylor, spokesman for the Motion Picture Association of America.
MPAA President Jack Valenti headed the group that developed the ratings, unveiled last month and already in place on broadcast and some cable networks.

Under last year's telecommunications law, the FCC will put the ratings out for public comment -- probably for 30 to 60 days -- and then decide whether to approve them. The agency has no formal timetable for making its decision.
If officials decide the system is unacceptable, the FCC must set up an advisory panel to devise a new one.
The television industry has vowed to fight any government-imposed plan in court on First Amendment grounds.
The age-based ratings -- such as TV-G for suitable for all ages and TV-PG for parental guidance suggested -- are similar to the 28-year-old system used by the motion-picture industry.

They have drawn criticism from some lawmakers, parent groups, children's advocates, educators and others who want a system that also would specify violence, sex and foul language using letters such as V, S and L.
President Clinton has asked that the new system be given a chance before attempts are made to change it, calling the ratings a "huge step forward over what we have now, which is nothing."
